title: A field extension in characteristic zero is formally smooth
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $K\supseteq k$ a field extension (with no finiteness condition). Then $K$ is formally smooth over $k$ (Stacks Algebra, Definition 00TI; the case $\mathfrak n=0$ of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]): for every commutative ring $D$ with a ring map $k\to D$, every ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, with quotient map $q:D\to D/J$, and every homomorphism of $k$-algebras $g:K\to D/J$, there is a homomorphism of $k$-algebras $f:K\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 0322 (proposition-characterize-separable-field-extensions, line 44475), characteristic-zero part, item (3) ($K$ is formally smooth over $k$)
